hypothesis: The three changes (A76 placement and admission, CPU clock option, in-line SGI with time-slice rule) meet the design budgets in host models and emulation
prediction:
Budgets set by the design (base value, target):
Default OS images, first commit: loadable bytes differ only in the default-affinity constant and the build identity. Call sites that place work on cores 6 or 7: three (recognizer, inference worker, GPU worker). A76 admission: 8 reads, no writes, once per boot; the clock build adds 22 inspection reads and 2 read-only PMIC snapshots. CPU-B raise with a voltage write: 5 clock register writes, 2 PMIC requests, 3 adapter DSB SY. Owner ticks while parked: 0 when the PLL locks in about 20 us; the model rejects a PLL write without the 20 us settle. Longest park: about 90 ms (10 ms update bound, 70 ms lock bound, 10 ms margin); RETAINED stays parked until the halt. Owner wake-ups added: 0. Transitions per boot: at most twice the grant's change count. Tick on core 0 that wakes no task (scheduler running), base 1,345 instructions median, 5 SVC, 28 DSB, 5 SGIs: at most 700 instructions, 0 SVC, at most 18 DSB, 0 SGIs. Receive work per tick on other cores: base 7 x (SGI handler 15 + vTaskSwitchContext 305 instructions), target 0. vInterruptCore from a handler, base 161 instructions, 1 SVC, 2 DSB, 1 ISB: at most 80, 0, 1, 0. EL0 send path (QEMU port): at most 5 instructions more than upstream vInterruptCore per EL0 send, with the QEMU EL0 round trip recorded under a regression guard of 24 instructions per send. Other QEMU port operations: none higher; EL1 round trip at most 12,191 instructions.
conclusion: Every budget with a target was met in host models and emulation; no board ran the image. The board-dependent budget (recognition time at the board's highest point) was not measured.
narrative:
Conditions. Base tree 15600aea (the integration branch merged into the package branch). Measured commits a0780792 (placement and admission), d3a44665 (clock option) and 4f5acef6 (in-line SGI and time slice), each with the package's primary.patch applied for the files outside the package (apps/mimus/parallel_runtime.*, apps/mimus/recorded.cc and the vInterruptCore hunk of patches/freertos-a733-smp.patch). Image comparisons: each tree extracted with git archive, copied over one shared source path and built in one shared build directory with clang 21 and the project toolchain file, so file-name strings and addresses match; a build from the worktree path gave the same ELF hash; functions compared by symbol size (nm -S). Cached instruction model: checks/a733-smp-cached.py --count from the measured tree, which counts vInterruptCore, xTaskIncrementTick and the SGI sends inside each counted call, run on the cached diagnostic of the base tree (built at f29c157c, whose kernel, port and diagnostic sources equal 15600aea's) and of 4f5acef6; figures are medians per call over the scheduler run, every task in that image at EL0. The baseline tick and SGI counts were taken on 2026-10-24 with that model. QEMU: checks/smp-port-cost.py from the measured tree, once with --root set to the base tree and once with --baseline and --round-trip-reduction 0; QEMU 10.2.1, -icount shift=0; Cortex-A55 and Cortex-A76 models gave identical counts. The host was shared with other work at a load average of 20 to 33 on 24 hardware threads.

Results (base -> measured; result):
Default OS images, first commit: supervised, resident, resident with microphone and resident with headset images differ by vTaskStartScheduler +4 bytes and the affinity immediate (#-1 to #0x3f) in task creation, mimus_transcribe_recorded +64 bytes for the CLOCK hook (prints nothing without the OS record), and the identity; met.
Call sites that place work on cores 6 or 7: recognizer (1 << 6), inference worker (1 << 7), GPU worker in the GPU build; every other task takes 0x3F; met.
A76 admission: as targeted, counted from the code; the model's inspection case writes no register and no PMIC byte; met.
CPU-B raise with a voltage write (A2 on board 3-3): 5 clock writes, 1 snapshot and 1 PMIC write, 3 DSB SY (code); met.
Owner ticks while parked: 0; parked 23 us of model time; 15 owner ticks for the whole transition; met. With a lock of 300 us: 1 parked tick, parked 1,203 us of model time (recorded).
Longest park: bounded by the 10 ms update, 70 ms lock and 10 ms margin limits (by construction). Owner wake-ups added: 0, the thermal task's per-tick loop is unchanged.
Tick on core 0 that wakes no task, scheduler running (16 base ticks, 9 measured): instructions median 1,345 -> 554, largest 1,667 -> 590, SVC 5 -> 0, DSB 28 -> 18, SGI sends 5 -> 0; met. Ticks that wake tasks: 36 ticks and 246 SGI sends over the run in the base, 47 and 177 measured (required preemptions, recorded). Ticks taken while the scheduler is suspended: 15 ticks and median 229 instructions in the base, 8 and 231 measured (recorded).
vInterruptCore from a handler: instructions, SVC, DSB, ISB 161, 1, 2, 1 -> 18, 0, 1, 0; met. SGI handler calls over the run 407 -> 185; vTaskSwitchContext calls 708 -> 480.
EL1 cross-core round trip (QEMU): 12,191 -> 11,994 instructions; met. EL0 send path: 5 instructions more than upstream (disassembly); met. EL0 cross-core round trip: 14,127 -> 14,169 (+21 per send, recorded; regression guard 24 per send). A control build with five no-ops in the base send path gave an EL0 round trip of 14,147 and an EL1 round trip of 12,240, that is 10 and 24 instructions per send: QEMU's lock-wait interleaving amplifies a longer send. Other QEMU port operations unchanged (met).
The tick rows come from the tick_by_wakes result of checks/a733-smp-cached.py --count, which sorts each tick by its prvYieldForTask entries and by whether the scheduler was suspended. The budget covers ticks that wake no task; in the base those ticks still sent five time-slice SGIs to cores whose same-priority peers are pinned elsewhere. An earlier comparison of the median of all ticks mixed pended and waking ticks and reported the budget as missed. Skipping the ready-list scan when a list is no longer than the cores running its priority was measured and left out: the zero-wake median rose to 618 instructions.

After the GPU recognition package merged (integration branch db7b77ce): with the A76 worker calls added to the GPU recognizer patch and primary.patch applied, the four default OS images were compared with the same images built from db7b77ce at one shared path. Only four functions differ: mimus_transcribe_recorded (1,868 to 1,932 bytes, the CLOCK hook), vTaskStartScheduler (564 to 568, the default-affinity constant), vInterruptCore (28 to 100, the in-line send) and xTaskIncrementTick (1,060 to 856, the time-slice rule). The default, A76 (supervised and resident), clock and GPU-linear builds, the last with and without A733_A76_ADMITTED, link and pass their link checks; with admission the GPU interrupt routes to core 6 and the image links the inference worker. checks/os-image-dispatch.py --configure-from on the GPU build, checks/os-image-launch.py on the default (21 cases) and clock (31) builds, checks/smp-sgi-send.py on the rebuilt cached diagnostic and checks/check-index.py --verify passed.

After the code review: the A733 SGI value is computed in line, so vInterruptCore is 120 bytes and the out-of-line a733_smp_sgi_value and a733_cpu_sgi1r (104 bytes) leave the images. Compared with db7b77ce at one shared path the four default images differ in mimus_transcribe_recorded (+64 bytes), vTaskStartScheduler (+4), vInterruptCore (28 to 120), xTaskIncrementTick (1,060 to 856) and those two removed functions. The default, A76, clock and GPU-linear builds link and pass their link checks; checks/os-image-dispatch.py --configure-from, checks/smp-sgi-send.py, checks/smp-port-cost.py, tools/check-smp.py kernel and context (ten trials on each CPU model), the soak under -icount and tools/check-mimus-smp.py passed again.

hypothesis: The clock transition model, OS image models, SMP checks and QEMU soak pass with the three changes
narrative:
All passed unless stated otherwise.
checks/cpu-clock-check.py with the extended model, whose clock runs in nanoseconds and returns whole microseconds: settle, inspection, burst, A2 and stopped-time-source cases. Altered drivers failed the model: no settle after the park, a settle that trusts its first quantized reading, a burst that polls once, and a burst without a poll bound, which never returns.
checks/os-image-model.c for the clock build: 37 refusals supervised and 58 with the microphone, including each grant-record rule and a grant of both clusters; a 2,002 MHz CPU-B grant for the session is admitted.
checks/os-image-launch.py: default supervised (22 cases) and clock build (34). The clock build adds the A2 preparation and eleven refusals, including a B1 record that did not pass or carried a grant, and every build refuses a link check whose cpu_clock record differs.
checks/os-image-audio.py on the supervised microphone build and the clock build with microphone; checks/os-image-headset.py on the resident A76 headset build; checks/reset-latency.py.
Builds and their link checks: the four default OS images, the A76 build supervised, resident and resident with headset, and the clock build supervised and with microphone. CMake refuses the clock option with the resident lifetime and without A733_A76_ADMITTED.
checks/smp-sgi-send.py on the measured cached diagnostic: four cases. On the base diagnostic it fails at the handler case, which takes SVC 117.
checks/a733-smp-cached.py --count: the eight-core scheduler run and the missing-secondary refusal pass on both diagnostics.
tools/check-smp.py kernel and context, ten trials each on cortex-a55 and cortex-a76.
tools/check-smp.py soak8 deviates from its gate of ten passing real-time trials per CPU model: under the host load above (load average 20 to 33 on 24 hardware threads), the real-time QEMU run failed in its first trial at the soak's one-second migration acknowledgement for both trees. Twenty alternating single trials passed 10 times for the base and 11 times for the measured tree, so the failures are not attributable to the change. Under -icount, which ties virtual time to instructions, the measured soak passed with shifts 0 to 4 on both CPU models, ten distinct schedules, before and after the review changes. These runs and the base comparison stand in for the real-time gate until a run on a lightly loaded host. With shifts 5 to 7 each instruction takes 32 to 128 ns of virtual time, and both trees fail the same one-second wait; the base passes at shifts 0 and 4 and fails at 5 and 7.
tools/check-mimus-smp.py on smp-mimus-model: features, log probabilities, frame count, words, punctuation, capitals and formatted text match the host reference, with the worker's cores at their defaults.

hypothesis: Recognition of the 8.87 s bench recording on the A76 pair, modeled per CPU-B point
prediction:
GPU recognition design models 0.818 s on the A76 pair at 2,002 MHz against the goal's 0.4435 s (0.05 times the audio duration). That figure needs a speed bin that admits 2,002 MHz (board 3-3 returned 0x00000496 at fuse word 0x0300624c: code 0x04, column vf0400, CPU-B up to 2,002 MHz at 1,050 mV; board 3-1 not read; other bins stop at 1,794 MHz (vf0100) or 1,612 MHz (vf0300, vf0600), code 0 at 1,508 MHz under the driver's envelope), a granted raise (the CPU-B rate boot0 leaves was not recorded), both A76 cores (one A76 at 2,002 MHz models at about 1.30 s: 0.739 s linear, 0.565 s other stages, so the inference worker runs on core 7), and one lifetime for both (the GPU linear build requires the resident lifetime; a grant needs the supervised lifetime because every change needs the user's approval before each run and the stage-2 loader stamps a fresh epoch on every boot, so a prepared grant cannot name a resident boot).
Model: the linear stage comes from placement.py --summary of the GPU package at ad0420c; the other stages scale 4.582 s on one A55 at 494 MHz, assuming perfect scaling over both cores and twice an A55's work per clock on an A76. Each row assumes a placement table generated for that rate; an image that runs below its table's rate does worse. The model ignores the DSU (L3) clock. The A55 pair at 494 MHz models at 3.438 s.
Table (CPU-B point; linear stage with the GPU table; other stages; recognition with the GPU table; times audio; CPU-only on the pair):
2,002 MHz: 0.535 s; 0.283 s; 0.818 s; 0.092; 1.20 s
1,794 MHz: 0.578 s; 0.315 s; 0.893 s; 0.101; 1.34 s
1,612 MHz: 0.627 s; 0.351 s; 0.978 s; 0.110; 1.49 s
1,508 MHz: 0.637 s; 0.375 s; 1.012 s; 0.114; 1.60 s
1,014 MHz: 0.755 s; 0.558 s; 1.313 s; 0.148; 2.37 s
CPU-only recognition on the pair (A2 runs the supervised build without the GPU): 14.894 s x 494 / (2 x 2 x f) + 0.283 s, about 1.20 s at 2,002 MHz. When recognition is CPU-bound, B1's time divided by A2's equals 2,002 MHz divided by B1's CPU-B rate; a smaller ratio shows a limit outside the cores, such as the DSU clock.
conclusion: Model only; the integrated OS image has not run on a board, so recognition time at any CPU-B point is unmeasured. The A76 admission alone does not reach the goal; it supplies the core placement and the clock that other levers assume.

hypothesis: Read-only part of B1 on board 3-3: speed-bin code, CPU-L, CPU-B and DSU PLL and mux words, pattern and LFM words, and the DCDC3 and DCDC5 selectors (board bundles 14 and 15)
narrative:
Bundle 14 read through FEL readl and bundle 15 through the qualified PMIC provider in a returning CPU0 image. Readings:
Speed bin: SID 0x0300624c = 0x496, decoded code 0x04, column 4.
CPU-B: PLL 0xf8802700, mux/P 0x03000000; source PLL, N = 39, P = 0: 1,014 MHz from the 26 MHz oscillator.
DSU: PLL 0xf8802600, mux/P 0x03010105; N = 38, P = 1: 494 MHz.
CPU-L: PLL 0xf8802600, mux/P 0x03010000: 494 MHz.
Pattern and LFM, CPU-L and CPU-B: +0x4 = 0, +0x8 = 0x30000000, +0x18 = 0x40000001; pattern type, pattern LFM enable and LFM ramp enable all clear.
DCDC3 and DCDC5: enable 0xff, selector 0x9e each; enabled, 800 mV each.
Prior ranks run in the same lifetime: ranks 1 to 4 and rank 9 (cold DDR s7-ddr, base kernel check s7-bb2-run, native USB s13-r9-usb). On port 3-1 on 2026-10-24, in one lifetime, the corrected rank 7 diagnostic returned and the rank 8 workload passed, after the CPU0-only preparation and the all-eight-core pre-scheduler; a later image of that lifetime delivered one timer interrupt to each secondary (docs/board-runbooks/rank-7-diagnosis.md). Port 3-3 has run neither.

hypothesis: B1: supervised A76 build with the CPU clock option and a grant of no cluster runs the recognizer on core 6 and the worker on core 7 with text and CRCs equal to the host reference
prediction: B1 shows the recognizer on core 6 and the worker on core 7 with text and CRCs equal to the host reference, every service reporting while the tick and SGIs use the in-line paths. It records the recognition time from counter ticks at boot0's CPU-B rate (about 2.10 s on the bench recording from the A2 estimate with f = 1,014), the CLOCK lines before and after it, the fuse code, the CPU-B PLL, mux, pattern and LFM words and the DCDC3 and DCDC5 readings. The FEL ROM return does not reset CPU-B, so the image refuses to start with CPU-B at any rate but boot0's 1014 MHz, which keeps the baseline at boot0's point. Prerequisites on the same board in one power cycle: ranks 1 to 5 and rank 9 (rank 5, the forced-stall return, is not yet run on port 3-3), ranks 7 and 8 passed, and the supervised integrated OS image prepared from a reviewed entry record (the thermal owner's facts from a fresh reading and the DDR reservation of the recognition inputs). The image takes over USB0 and ends the session, so it runs last and the board then needs a power removal. B1 must pass with a grant of no cluster before any A step; its record has schema a733-os-cpu-clock-b1-v1.
conclusion: Not yet run: no integrated OS image has run on a board.
narrative: Planned run, listed under open work in the design; see the prediction for inputs and prerequisites.

hypothesis: A1, A2 and A3: granted CPU-B and CPU-L raises in the supervised A76 build, each after B1 passed on the same board
prediction:
Each step needs the user's explicit approval before the run, runs last in a connection window after B1 passed on that board, and is specific to that board through its approval record (schema a733-os-cpu-clock-approval-v1: board identity and port, image SHA-256, session epoch, generation and lease, the step, the cluster, the highest point, the change count, the approval text and date, and a reference to that board's B1 record showing the bin code, DCDC3 and DCDC5 readings and clear pattern and LFM words).
A1: CPU-B to 1,196 MHz, which needs 800 mV in every bin; the driver writes a voltage only if DCDC3 is below that. The first park and relock of a running cluster.
A2: CPU-B to the highest point of the board's bin (2,002 MHz at 1,050 mV on board 3-3), with the DCDC3 write and the ramp of 250 mV / 250 uV per us = 1 ms, and recognition timed at that point. The recognizer starts the timed run only after the clock owner has finished its requests, and the CLOCK lines before and after the run show the point and the largest parked interval. CPU-only recognition on the A76 pair: 14.894 s x 494 / (2 x 2 x 2,002) for the linear stage plus 0.283 s for the other stages, about 1.20 s at 2,002 MHz. B1's time divided by A2's equals 2,002 MHz divided by B1's CPU-B rate when recognition is CPU-bound.
A3 (optional): CPU-L to 1,196 MHz, the first trial that docs/cpu-clock.md names, for the service cores.
conclusion: Not yet run. The step-7 runs of docs/designs/cpu-top-opp.md (B1, then TOP) supersede A2 as the planned raise.
narrative: Planned runs, listed under open work in the design; see the prediction for the approval record fields and the figures.
